title: Sales Enablement: Complete Sales Kit — Positioning, Decks, Pricing, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: Provide a single, consumable sales kit for Redwood Inference AEs, SDRs, and solutions engineers covering positioning and messaging, competitive differentiators, recommended pitch decks and talking points, pricing guidance and SKU map, two concise customer case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this page when prepping discovery, technical deep-dive, or procurement conversations.

TL;DR messaging (lead):
- Redwood Inference is the developer-first inference platform that makes high-performance, cost-predictable LLM serving simple across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Value props: predictable latency & throughput, cost controls (batching/quantization), unified operational tooling, and enterprise-grade private deployment options.

1) Positioning & Core Messaging

Primary audience: ML & software engineers, platform teams, and product leads evaluating inference for production LLM features.

Key pillars (use as 30/60/90-second hooks):
- Production-first performance: measurable latency SLOs (e.g., p95 < 200ms on typical 1k token requests for dedicated instances), auto-batching, KV prefix caching to reduce per-token cost.
- Cost predictability & optimization: recommendations for quantization profiles and batching that reduce per-token cost 2–5x for common workloads; reserved Dedicated plans for predictable unit economics.
- Deployment flexibility: same API and toolchain across Hosted, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem) — no re-engineering for migration.
- Developer velocity: simple REST/SDK, streaming responses, function/tool-calling primitives, curated model catalog with verified performance profiles.

Elevator pitch (customer-ready):
"If you're building LLM features, Redwood gives you consistent production inference: the same API, predictable latency and unit costs, and an ops + observability layer so your engineering team can move fast without building a custom serving stack."

Messaging by persona (short bullets):
- Engineering/ML: focus on runtime performance, kernel/quantization recommendations, profiling hooks, SDK examples, and model variants.
- Platform/Infra: emphasize Dedicated capacity, autoscaling policies, region-aware routing, and SLA-backed latency/uptime targets.
- Security/Compliance: highlight Private deployment, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and SOC/ISO attestation roadmap.
- Product/PM: show cost per feature, A/B rollback, and quality monitoring tied to prompt sets.

2) Competitive Briefs — quick takeaways

Competitors to mention: public LLM APIs, cloud-managed model endpoints, self-hosted inference runtimes.

How Redwood compares (one-line bullets):
- vs. general cloud AI platforms: Redwood is inference-first with deeper runtime optimizations and cost controls; cloud endpoints provide model access but not the same cost/latency tooling.
- vs. simple LLM APIs: Redwood targets production economics and ops; many APIs are great for prototyping but lack dedicated capacity and private deployment options.
- vs. inference infrastructure vendors: Redwood delivers a managed control plane + unified API, removing heavy integration work.

Competitive playbook (tips for objections):
1. "We can just deploy open source models ourselves." — Acknowledge tradeoffs; emphasize total cost of ownership: scheduling, batching, kernel tuning, observability, and upgrades. Offer a TCO comparison template.
2. "Cloud provider endpoints are simpler." — Push on multi-environment parity and long-term cost: Redwood's Dedicated & caching features frequently reduce per-token cost and risk of platform lock-in.
3. "Security/governance is a blocker." — Share Private deployment reference architecture, KMS integrations, and recent SOC2/ISO artifacts. Offer a technical workshop.

3) Recommended Pitch Deck Structure (12–18 slides)

1. Cover: Redwood logo, one-line value prop.
2. Problem: operational challenges of production inference.
3. Solution: Redwood high-level.
4. How it works (1): serving runtime & optimizations (batching, KV cache).
5. How it works (2): deployment modes (Hosted / Dedicated / Private).
6. Performance benchmarks: example p50/p95 numbers and throughput for typical models.
7. Cost story: example per-feature cost before/after optimization.
8. Reliability & observability: Console screenshots (token breakdown, traces).
9. Security & compliance: Private options, KMS, audit logs.
10. Customer stories: 2 short case studies.
11. Pricing & licensing: snapshot with recommended SKUs.
12. Next steps & trial offer: pilot checklist, decision criteria, contacts.

Slide best practices: include one concrete benchmark per slide; show assumptions (sequence length, batch size). Keep technical appendix with kernel/quantization details for SE/ML audiences. Attach a 1-page one-pager for executives.

4) Pricing Guidance & SKU Map (sales-level summary)

Pricing principles: transparent usage for Hosted, committed/flat-fee for Dedicated, and platform licensing for Private. Offer optional addons: extended observability retention, premium SLA, and enterprise support.

Suggested SKUs and guidance (example):
- Hosted API (usage): per-token generation + per-embedding unit. Example: $0.003 per 1k input tokens / $0.012 per 1k output tokens for a standard Llama-variant (illustrative only).
- Dedicated (committed): base monthly commitment for reserved GPU pool + overage per token/compute-hour. Example tiers: "Dedicated-S" (4 GPUs) "Dedicated-M" (16 GPUs) "Dedicated-L" (64 GPUs).
- Private (license): annual platform fee + per-node runtime support; optional on-prem packaging and professional services.
- Add-ons: Enhanced observability (30/90/365 day retention), managed migration, security package with HSM integrations.

Pricing negotiation tips: front-load demo with cost comparisons for expected QPS and sequence lengths; offer 3–6 month pilot discounts with a technical SLA. For Dedicated deals, use usage envelopes and auto-burst policies to reduce overprovision risk.

Note: Exact numbers are governed by Finance; use this page for guidance and examples only. For legal/contract language, link to finance-and-legal contract templates.

5) Two Customer Case Studies (concise)

Case study A — Conversational Support Platform (B2B SaaS)
- Problem: Erratic latency and high serving costs after moving from prototype to production.
- Solution: Redwood Dedicated with KV prefix caching and quantization recommendations.
- Outcome: p95 latency reduced from 600ms to 180ms; token cost reduced by ~2.6x; achieved 99.95% uptime SLA.
- Timeline & ownership: Pilot (6 weeks) → Dedicated onboarding (8 weeks) → full rollout (3 months).

Case study B — Financial Services Knowledge Base (regulated workload)
- Problem: Data residency and auditability requirements; needed on-prem option.
- Solution: Private deployment (VPC + HSM-backed KMS) and single-tenant control plane; integrated with customer SSO and audit pipelines.
- Outcome: Passed external audit for access controls; enabled secure LLM features for 5000 agents; closed $1.2M contract.

6) Security FAQ for Prospects (top questions + concise answers)

Q: What deployment options meet strict data residency needs?
A: Private deployment supports VPC and on-prem packaging; customers can host the control plane and runtime within their network. We provide deployment reference architecture and professional services.

Q: How do you handle keys and secrets?
A: Integrations with customer-managed KMS/HSMs (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, customer HSMs). We provide end-to-end guidance and testing for key rotation policies.

Q: Is customer data logged or used to train models?
A: For Hosted customers who opt-in to data sharing, data usage is disclosed in contract; for Dedicated and Private customers, data is not used to train models by default. Audit logs and retention policies are configurable.

Q: Can we restrict access and enforce least privilege?
A: Yes — RBAC integrations, SSO (SAML/OIDC), and fine-grained API key scopes are supported. We also provide audit trails for all control-plane operations.

Q: What compliance artifacts do you provide?
A: SOC2 Type II report (available under NDA), data processing addendums, and guidance for ISO attestation plans. For Private customers we provide architecture and implementation evidence packages.

Q: What happens when an incident affects model outputs (hallucinations)?
A: We recommend prompt-level guardrails, eval/benchmark sets, and deployable quality monitors that trigger rollbacks. Our Console supports alerting tied to evaluation regressions and A/B rollout policies.

7) Sales Playbook: Trial → Pilot → Procurement (quick checklist)

Discovery (SDR/AE):
- Validate persona, QPS, typical sequence length, latency expectations, regulatory requirements.
- Identify primary success metric (latency budget, cost/go-live threshold, compliance gates).

Technical pilot (SE):
1. Offer a 4–6 week pilot: sample traffic ingestion, one or two representative prompts, and baseline benchmarks.
2. Deliver: latency/throughput report, cost-savings projection, and integration guide.
3. Provide a 1-day architecture workshop for Dedicated/Private prospects.

Procurement (AE + Finance):
- Use pre-approved contract templates; align on committed capacity and pilot conversion triggers; present add-on SKUs.
